Subject: Initial ask: model footprints + preferred quality knobs for dedicated sizing

Hi Kara — good to chat earlier. As promised, I'm pulling together a concise sizing playbook so your platform team can evaluate a Dedicated pool commitment without surprises. To produce a practical headroom estimate we need three things from your end: 

1) canonical model variants you expect to serve (name + peak prompt length). e.g. "owl-70b-32k" vs a 16k variant.
2) expected steady-state QPS and burst concurrency (p95 and peak minute).
3) whether you want inference at FP16, Q4_0/Q4_1, or to test Q5/Q8 quant profiles (tradeoff: lower memory but potential quality delta).

Quick notes on what we'll deliver: a per-variant GPU memory map (base model weights + KV cache sizing by context length), a suggested quantization profile per workload, and a recommended committed pod count with headroom for KV growth and soft-fallbacks.

If you can drop the model roster and a sample request profile (even a small CSV) we'll turn this into a one-pager with numbers by tomorrow EOD. Attaching a simple template for the memory profile you can fill: axion_memory_profile_v1.xlsx (stub).

Thanks,
Sean

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Kara Liu <kara.liu@axionlabs.ai>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Axion Labs GPU headroom allocation playbook — draft calculations

Sean / Karthik — quick pass on numbers from Kara's profile. High level assumptions:
- Model weights (orca-70b fp32) ~ 280GB; FP16 will halve that to ~140GB. With Sharded loading (two-GPU mirrored shards) and tensor-parallel optimizations we expect ~72–80GB per GPU for base weights depending on kernel packing; using quant Q4_1 for weights cuts it to ~45–50GB.
- KV cache sizing rule: ~ (sequence_length * hidden_size * 2 bytes) per token for fp16 KV entries. For orca-70b hidden_size 12288:
  * 6k tokens -> KV ~ 6,000 * 12,288 * 2 ≈ 147MB? (note: this is per layer factor — we should multiply by number of layers; more accurate calc below)
  * Practical measured KV overhead (end-to-end) for 70B/32k variant at 6k tokens: ~40–48GB across all layers on a single inference instance. At 18k tokens p95 that pushes KV to ~120–140GB.

- Concurrency math (steady 12 qps, p95 concurrency 60): if we pair 1 GPU serving ~6 simultaneous contexts at target latency, we'd need ~10–12 GPUs for steady. But headroom for burst (250) implies spindle to 40–50 GPUs if all streams push long context windows simultaneously.

Sizing recommendation (initial committed Dedicated pool):
- Commit 16 A100-class GPUs for the first 3 months, configured with mixed-precision FP16 for baseline. Rationale: supports steady qps with comfortable headroom for p95 context growth and allows room for model weight placement and KV cache during spikes via autoscaling/burst.
- Optional aggressive option (cost-saving): commit 12 GPUs but enable Q4_1 on orca-70b for non-critical routes and push longer-context sessions to a higher-tier pod. This reduces per-GPU model footprint by ~35–40% but requires evals on quality.

Attachments: initial-sizing-estimate.csv (contains per-variant GPU memo and headroom margins).

I'll run a micro-sim with 18k token p95 and get a tighter headroom number — aiming to have that out within 6 hours.

— Marcus
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-24T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Axion Labs GPU headroom allocation playbook — next steps and MAP

Kara — thanks for the quick details and Marcus for the calc. Attached is a one-page playbook PDF that summarizes the recommendation and a proposed mutual action plan (MAP). Highlights: 

- Baseline commit: 16 A100-class GPUs (FP16) for initial 3-month reserved pool. Autoscale to 48 GPUs for peak-minute bursts (pay-as-you-go burst) — this keeps the committed cost reasonable while meeting 250 concurrent stream spikes.
- Fallback strategy: routes with strict quality keep FP16; bulk batch/low-priority routes can be Q4_1. We'll include a per-route routing policy in the playbook.
- Sizing caveat: if Axion moves to a primary 32k context runtime for 70B by default, we should re-evaluate headroom because KV memory becomes dominant; in that case we recommend staged KV offload (NVMe-backed) for the largest sessions and a higher reserved commit.

Next steps / action items:
1) Kara: confirm whether Retrieval RAG flows require 32k context by default or only for a small minority of sessions (reply by EOD Friday).
2) Redwood (Marcus + Karthik): deliver a micro-sim with 18k token p95 run and a per-route latency/cost table (ETA: 24 hours).
3) Procurement (Axion): share PO timeline and any contract constraints (SLA/region).

If that timeline works I'll draft a short appendix for procurement showing expected monthly committed cost vs burst cost.

Thanks,
Sean
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
